Amritsar: The city shaped around the sacred pool

Founded in the late sixteenth century around the Amrit Sarovar, Amritsar grew into a major spiritual, commercial and cultural centre. Its story is closely connected with the Sikh Gurus and the development of Harmandir Sahib.
Harmandir Sahib · Jallianwala Bagh · Gobindgarh Fort · old bazaars
Sikh sacred architecture, langar and seva, the 1919 massacre and its remembrance, traditional markets, foodways and borderland life.
Barnala: A Malwa town with a rural heart

Barnala sits in the Malwa region, where town life is closely connected to surrounding agricultural villages. Its place record will trace the changing relationship between mandi culture, farming communities and the everyday Punjabi language of the region.
Malwa settlement · agricultural markets · village life
Agriculture and land use, local markets, village institutions, folk performance, changing crafts and oral histories.
Bathinda: An old crossroads of the southern Punjab plains

Bathinda has a long recorded past. Government district history records earlier forms of the name including Tabarhindh and Batrind, while the district’s heritage reflects Sikh, Hindu and Muslim histories.
Qila Mubarak · Takht Sri Damdama Sahib · Maiser Khana
Fort history, Sikh religious heritage, shared sacred places, Malwa agriculture, local memory and historic routes.
Faridkot: A princely-state legacy in the Malwa

Faridkot’s modern identity is linked with the former princely state of Faridkot and the wider Malwa landscape. Its historic buildings and public institutions offer a way to read the region’s changing political and social history.
Qila Mubarak · royal-era buildings · rural Malwa
Princely administration, architecture, Sufi and Sikh traditions, farming communities and local music.
Fatehgarh Sahib: Fatehgarh Sahib holds a central place in Sikh historical memory, especially the martyrdom of the younger Sahibzade at Sirhind. The district’s heritage is inseparable from remembrance, pilgrimage and the layered history of the Sirhind region.
Gurdwara Fatehgarh Sahib · Aam Khas Bagh · Sirhind
Sikh history, Mughal-era Sirhind, pilgrimage practices, historic waterworks and community remembrance.
Fazilka: A borderland shaped by river, canal and field

Fazilka lies in the south-western border region of Indian Punjab. Its landscapes and settlements are shaped by agriculture, canal irrigation, cross-border histories and the cultural life of the Fazilka-Firozpur belt.
Asafwala War Memorial · border villages · canal colonies
Borderland memory, farming and irrigation, migration, local markets, crafts and oral accounts.
Ferozepur: A frontier town with layered military and freedom histories

Ferozepur’s position near the India–Pakistan border has shaped its strategic and social history. Its heritage includes Sikh sites, colonial-era military traces and places connected with India’s freedom movement.
National Martyrs Memorial, Hussainiwala · Saragarhi Memorial · cantonment
Freedom movement memory, military history, Sikh heritage, border communities and riverine landscapes.
Gurdaspur: The upper doab between rivers and hills

Gurdaspur occupies a varied landscape between the Ravi and Beas river systems and the foothills to the north. Its towns and villages connect agrarian life with pilgrimage routes and older settlement histories.
Dera Baba Nanak · Batala · historic gurdwaras
Sikh pilgrimage, river landscapes, old market towns, agriculture, craft traditions and border histories.
Hoshiarpur: Shivalik foothills, archaeology and skilled hands

At the edge of the Shivalik foothills, Hoshiarpur’s heritage connects prehistoric archaeology with living craft traditions. The district administration highlights Dholbaha’s archaeological record and the region’s distinctive inlay work.
Gandhara-era finds, foothill ecology, wood inlay, trade between hills and plains, village traditions.
Jalandhar: A historic doab city of sport, craft and commerce

Jalandhar lies in the fertile Doaba region and has developed as an important centre of trade, education, sport-goods manufacturing and religious life. Its modern identity is rooted in a much older network of towns and villages.
Devi Talab Temple · old city markets · rural Doaba
Doaba settlement, sports manufacturing, religious architecture, migration, music and market culture.
Kapurthala: A princely city of distinctive architecture

Kapurthala’s princely-state past is visible in its palaces, civic buildings and planned urban spaces. Its architectural record includes European-inspired forms alongside Punjabi and Sikh religious heritage.
Jagatjit Palace · Moorish Mosque · Shalimar Gardens · Sultanpur Lodhi
Princely architecture, Sultanpur Lodhi and Sikh history, gardens, urban planning and craft.
Ludhiana: Industrial energy rooted in the central Punjab countryside

Ludhiana grew from a historic settlement into one of Punjab’s major industrial and commercial centres. The city’s story links the old town and Sutlej-side landscape with textiles, bicycle manufacturing and the agricultural economy.
Lodhi-era old town · Punjab Agricultural University Museum · rural Sutlej belt
Industrial craft, textiles, bicycles, agricultural research, migration and changing urban life.
Malerkotla: A distinctive history of coexistence and community

Malerkotla has a distinctive place in Punjab’s social history, shaped by its former princely state, Muslim cultural heritage and traditions of inter-community relations. Its story deserves to be documented through local voices as well as monuments.
Sheesh Mahal · Mubarak Manzil · historic mosques and bazaars
Nawabi-era architecture, Punjabi Muslim traditions, shared civic life, poetry, food and oral histories.
Mansa: The cotton belt and folk culture of southern Malwa

Mansa is part of the southern Malwa region, where cotton cultivation, village economies and Punjabi folk traditions shape everyday life. Its heritage is found as much in farms and local memory as in built landmarks.
Mansa town · rural cotton belt · village fairs
Cotton and agriculture, folk songs, oral histories, village architecture and changing livelihoods.
Moga: A rural heartland of the central Malwa

Moga’s district identity is closely connected with farming settlements and the wider Malwa region. Its local history can be explored through village institutions, agrarian change, religious places and the everyday culture of its market towns.
Moga town · village gurdwaras · agricultural landscape
Agrarian life, village histories, religious traditions, folk performance and migration.
Pathankot: A gateway between Punjab, Jammu and the hills

Pathankot occupies a strategic position where Punjab meets the foothills and routes towards Jammu and Himachal Pradesh. The district’s landscape and history are shaped by movement, defence, trade and nearby historic religious sites.
Mukteshwar Temple · Ranjit Sagar region · Shahpur Kandi
Foothill geography, historic routes, temples and shrines, defence history and river landscapes.
Patiala: The cultural imprint of a former princely state

Patiala was one of the prominent princely states of the former Punjab. Its royal-era architecture, music traditions and institutions give the city a distinctive place in the region’s cultural history.
Qila Mubarak · Sheesh Mahal · Moti Bagh Palace
Phulkari and craft, Patiala gharana, royal architecture, urban history and surrounding village culture.
Rupnagar: Rupnagar, also known as Ropar, is associated with an important archaeological site on the Sutlej. Its wider district landscape includes riverine settlements, the Shivalik edge and places connected with Sikh history.
Rupnagar archaeological site · Anandpur Sahib · Bhakra reservoir region
Indus-era archaeology, Sutlej ecology, Sikh history, river engineering and foothill communities.
S.A.S. Nagar (Mohali): A planned city beside an older cultural landscape

S.A.S. Nagar, commonly known as Mohali, is a planned urban centre adjoining Chandigarh. Its contemporary growth sits within a landscape of older villages, Sikh institutions and the wider historic region around Ropar and the foothills.
Gurudwara Amb Sahib · Silvi Park · nearby village settlements
Planned urban development, village histories, Sikh institutions, sport and changing peri-urban life.
Sangrur: Royal-era memory across the Malwa plains
Sangrur’s heritage reflects the princely state of Jind and the wider Malwa region. Its historic buildings, gardens and nearby religious centres provide a record of changing political and social life.
Banasar Garden · Sheesh Mahal · Bhai Gurdas birthplace tradition
Princely history, architecture, folk traditions, agriculture and the cultural geography of Malwa.
Shaheed Bhagat Singh Nagar: Doaba villages and the memory of revolution

Shaheed Bhagat Singh Nagar, formerly Nawanshahr district, carries a strong association with the freedom movement and the Doaba region. Its villages, memorial sites and migration histories connect local life with wider Punjabi and global stories.
Khatkar Kalan · Nawanshahr town · Doaba villages
Bhagat Singh’s legacy, freedom movement memory, village histories, migration and agrarian culture.
Sri Muktsar Sahib: A landscape of Sikh courage and remembrance

Sri Muktsar Sahib is closely associated with the Battle of Muktsar in 1705 and the memory of the Chali Mukte. The district’s cultural life also reflects the agricultural rhythms and folk traditions of south-western Punjab.
Gurdwara Tuti Gandi Sahib · Muktsar Sarovar · historic battle sites
Sikh history, pilgrimage, oral remembrance, Malwa folk culture and farming.
Tarn Taran: A sacred town and the Majha countryside

Tarn Taran is known for the historic sarovar and gurdwara established in the Sikh period. The district’s wider Majha landscape connects religious history with agriculture, village life and the border region.
Gurdwara Sri Tarn Taran Sahib · Goindwal Sahib · border villages
Sikh sacred architecture, sarovar traditions, Majha dialect and culture, farming and borderland memory.
Lahore: The cultural heart of historic Punjab

Lahore’s walled city preserves layers of Mughal, Sikh and colonial-era history. Its monumental architecture, bazaars, gardens, food culture and literary life make it one of the defining cultural centres of Punjab.
Lahore Fort · Shalimar Gardens · Wazir Khan Mosque · Walled City
Mughal urbanism, Sikh-era landmarks, Sufi shrines, craft bazaars, foodways and literary culture.
Multan: The city of saints and blue pottery

Multan is one of the historic centres of southern Punjab, widely known for its Sufi shrines and long-standing craft traditions. Its old urban fabric, shrines and bazaars reflect centuries of religious, artistic and commercial exchange.
Shrine of Shah Rukn-e-Alam · Bahauddin Zakariya · Hussain Agahi Bazaar
Sufi heritage, blue pottery, camel-skin craft, mango cultivation, bazaars and historic urban form.
Rawalpindi: A garrison city at the edge of the Potohar plateau

Rawalpindi grew as a major military and commercial centre in northern Punjab. Its bazaars, railway-era buildings and cantonment landscape reflect the city’s role as a meeting point between the plains and routes towards the hills.
Raja Bazaar · Rawalpindi Railway Station · old cantonment
Potohar culture, colonial-era urbanism, bazaars, transport history and nearby hill routes.
Faisalabad: Lyallpur’s planned grid and textile heritage

Faisalabad was laid out as Lyallpur during the colonial canal-colony period. Its distinctive eight-road clock-tower plan and later growth as a textile and industrial centre connect the city to the agricultural transformation of central Punjab.
Clock Tower and eight bazaars · Lyallpur Museum · canal-colony landscape
Canal-colony settlement, textile production, agricultural markets, migration and industrial labour.
Gujranwala: A city of wrestling, food and Sikh-era history

Gujranwala is associated with the early life of Maharaja Ranjit Singh and has grown into a major industrial and food centre. Its story links Sikh-era history with the craft, trade and sporting traditions of central Punjab.
Ranjit Singh’s birthplace tradition · old bazaars · nearby Eminabad
Sikh history, wrestling akharas, food culture, industry and old market networks.
Sialkot: A historic city of learning, craft and sport

Sialkot has a long history as a centre of trade and skilled manufacture. Today it is internationally associated with sports goods and surgical instruments, while its older cultural landscape includes literary, religious and educational traditions.
Iqbal Manzil · Sialkot Fort remains · historic bazaars
Allama Iqbal’s legacy, sports-goods craft, surgical instruments, education and borderland culture.
Gujrat: The Chenab-side city of pottery and furniture craft

Gujrat lies in the Chenab region and is known for its pottery and furniture industries. Its history connects river crossings, old settlements and artisan skills with the wider commercial networks of northern Punjab.
Chenab river landscape · old Gujrat bazaars · artisan workshops
Pottery, furniture making, river trade, village craft clusters and local food traditions.
Jhelum: Fortresses, river routes and the Salt Range

Jhelum’s district landscape stretches from the Jhelum River towards the Salt Range. It contains major historic sites, including Rohtas Fort, as well as Khewra’s salt-mining heritage and older religious and archaeological locations.
Rohtas Fort · Khewra Salt Mine · Tilla Jogian
Fortification and military history, salt mining, Potohar landscapes, archaeology and pilgrimage.
Sargodha: The citrus belt of central Punjab

Sargodha is widely associated with kinnow citrus cultivation and the agricultural economy of central Punjab. Its modern growth is closely tied to farming, irrigation, military history and the development of planned settlements.
Kirana Hills · citrus-growing belt · old Sargodha cantonment
Citrus horticulture, irrigation, rural markets, geological landscape and migration.
Bahawalpur: The former princely state beside the Cholistan desert

Bahawalpur was the capital of a princely state whose legacy remains visible in palaces, civic buildings and the desert-edge landscape. The nearby Cholistan region preserves pastoral traditions and the monumental Derawar Fort.
Noor Mahal · Darbar Mahal · Derawar Fort · Cholistan
Nawabi architecture, desert pastoralism, forts, camel culture, embroidery and Sufi heritage.
Bahawalnagar: Canal landscapes and the eastern desert fringe

Bahawalnagar lies in the south-eastern part of Pakistani Punjab, where irrigated agricultural land meets the wider Cholistan desert environment. Its local record centres on settlement, farming, water and borderland communities.
Canal irrigation, desert-edge livelihoods, pastoral memory, village histories and crafts.
Dera Ghazi Khan: The meeting of the Indus plain and the Sulaiman foothills

Dera Ghazi Khan sits between the Indus plain and the Sulaiman mountain front. Its cultural geography includes riverine settlements, tribal and pastoral traditions, and routes linking the plains with the western highlands.
Fort Munro · Indus river belt · Taunsa region
Mountain and plain exchange, pastoral life, Sufi shrines, river ecology and local languages.
Muzaffargarh: Between the Chenab and Indus rivers

Muzaffargarh occupies the doab between the Chenab and Indus rivers. Its heritage is closely connected to riverine agriculture, canal development, settlement patterns and the communities who live with seasonal water changes.
Chenab–Indus doab · Alipur · historic river settlements
River ecology, agriculture, irrigation, flood memory, local crafts and village oral histories.
Attock: A historic crossing at the Indus

Attock’s strategic position at the Indus crossing has made it important to movement and defence across northern Punjab. The district’s history is connected with forts, river routes, the Potohar plateau and colonial-era transport links.
Attock Fort · Attock Khurd railway station · Indus crossing
River crossings, military architecture, railway history, Potohar culture and trade routes.
Chiniot: Master craftsmanship carved into wood and stone

Chiniot is celebrated for its carved wooden furniture, ornate havelis and skilled artisan workshops. Set near the Chenab, the city’s craft heritage reflects generations of specialist knowledge and a strong bazaar culture.
Umar Hayat Mahal · Shahi Mosque · Chenab riverfront
Wood carving, furniture making, stonework, merchant havelis and artisan lineages.
Rahim Yar Khan: A southern gateway between river and desert

Rahim Yar Khan lies in the southern Punjab region between the Indus-side agricultural belt and the Cholistan desert. Its settlements reflect a mix of canal agriculture, desert-edge livelihoods and historic routes.
Pattan Minara · Bhong Mosque · desert-edge settlements
Archaeological memory, mosque architecture, cotton and date cultivation, pastoral life.
Kasur: The city of Bulleh Shah and Punjabi Sufi poetry

Kasur is strongly associated with the Sufi poet Bulleh Shah, whose poetry remains central to Punjabi literary and musical culture. The city’s shrines, old neighbourhoods and food traditions form an important part of the Lahore–Kasur cultural corridor.
Shrine of Bulleh Shah · old Kasur bazaars · border region
Sufi poetry, kafi singing, shrine culture, traditional food and borderland life.
Sheikhupura: Mughal-era hunting grounds and garden architecture

Sheikhupura’s best-known heritage includes Hiran Minar, a Mughal-era complex associated with Emperor Jahangir. The district’s historic landscape also includes a fort and settlements linked to the Lahore region.
Hiran Minar · Sheikhupura Fort · Mughal-era landscape
Mughal architecture, water engineering, gardens, local agriculture and regional trade.
Sahiwal: The modern gateway to the ancient city of Harappa

Sahiwal district is the modern administrative setting for Harappa, one of the major archaeological sites of the Indus Civilization. Its heritage links ancient urban life with the canal-colony era and the agricultural communities of central Punjab.
Harappa archaeological site · Harappa Museum · canal-colony settlements
Indus Civilization, archaeology, museum collections, canal colonies and farming.
Okara: A canal-colony landscape of farms and market towns

Okara’s modern agricultural landscape developed through irrigation and canal-colony settlement. Its towns and villages reflect the transformation of the central Punjab plains into an intensive farming region.
Renala Khurd · Ravi-side landscape · agricultural markets
Canal irrigation, dairy and crop farming, colonial-era settlement, village crafts and oral histories.
Chakwal: Salt Range temples, forts and Potohar traditions

Chakwal sits within the Potohar and Salt Range cultural landscape. Its heritage includes the Katas Raj temple complex, historic forts and village traditions shaped by the rocky plateau and seasonal water sources.
Katas Raj Temples · Malot Fort · Salt Range
Religious architecture, geology, pastoral livelihoods, village customs and historic routes.
Mianwali: The Indus frontier and the Salt Range edge

Mianwali’s landscape brings together the Indus River, the Salt Range and the dry uplands of north-western Punjab. Its cultural record includes river communities, pastoral life and the region’s distinctive Seraiki-Punjabi linguistic mix.
Kalabagh · Namal Lake · Indus river belt
River and upland ecology, pastoral traditions, local languages, crafts and settlement histories.
